newsitem.title: HONG KONG: TENNIS-WRIST INJURY KEEPS SAMPRAS FROM HK OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-WRIST INJURY KEEPS SAMPRAS FROM HK OPEN.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras has withdrawn from next week's Hong Kong Open Tennis because of a wrist injury, robbing the tournament of one of its biggest names and leaving American Michael Chang as the favourite.

"While we regret Pete will not be able to come to Hong Kong, we understand that injuries are part of professional sports. We hope he will make a speedy recovery," tournament director Michael Luevano told reporters on Thursday night.
Sampras, injured in a Key Biscayne, Florida, championship last month, had also decided to pull out of the Japan Open starting on April 14 to undergo therapy.
Chang will be promoted to number one seed in the Hong Kong meeting, giving him a chance to win his fourth Hong Kong Open.
"I think in any tournament it would be great to get the world's number one. I would like to have met Sampras in the final," Chang said on his arrival on Thursday night.
"It's premature to say how well I'm going to do. I will always play my best. This year is no exception. I have prepared for it well but the tournament still looks very strong."
